title: Can an LLM agent detect and repair a planted shortcut in a genomics CNN without data? A preregistered, blinded test of weight-space programming
read_level: full (preprint reports/preprint/main.pdf from the release zip, main text and limitations; appendices skimmed; other release files not read)
metadata_mismatch: Zenodo record title is 'Weight-space programming on a regulatory-genomics CNN: public release 1' (software/data release, version 1.0.1, version record 24040592); the enclosed preprint has the title used here. Corpus metadata abstract was empty. Author matches.
why_wsp: Claude Opus 5.5 sessions in Claude Code read the weights of a 58k-parameter CTCF-binding CNN to name a planted shortcut with no forward passes, then submit repaired weights with 0 or 50 metered forward passes, without gradients or data.
domain: regulatory genomics (CTCF binding CNN; planted backdoor-like shortcuts)
editor: Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5, effort high) in Claude Code v2.1.318
target: small CNN, 58,433 parameters (18 planted, 10 clean models)
interface: code/tensor tools (CPU Python over weights.npz in sandbox; fp_query metered forward passes; wsp_submit)
loop: one-shot for detection (phase A, 0 passes); closed-loop with feedback for repair at budget 50 (median 7.5 passes used)
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: 'edits were small (0.1–7.7% of weights)' (Sec 4); only 12 of 56 sessions changed weights

headline_results.quote: The primary hypothesis (detection more often than false alarms) was supported, but narrowly: D = 0.396 [0.021, 0.792], one-sided p = 0.0177.

headline_results.claim: Detection by instance; no false alarms
headline_results.quote: Two of four planted patterns were found in 3 of 4 answers each, the third k-mer never, and the poly-A pattern once in 12; no clean model drew a false alarm.
By arithmetic on the preregistered bootstrap, the support rests on that single poly-A answer.

headline_results.claim: Budget 0 sessions ran local forward computation; all correct detections came from them
headline_results.quote: 47 of 56 sessions ran parts of the network locally (on synthetic activations or constructed inputs), and all 7 correct detections came from such sessions.

headline_results.claim: Per-protocol analyses do not support detection
headline_results.quote: PP1 (32 cells) gives D = 0.406 [0.000, 0.850], p = 0.0341, not supported
Repair largely failed: 2 of 36 planted-model sessions met the fix criterion, though 7 of 8 k-mer edits removed over 93% of the shortcut's effect on the probe
Every edit kept clean AUPRC within the limit (largest drop 0.0009).
Stated confidence was 0.6–0.8 for 49 answers, of which 51% were correct, and above 0.8 for 7, all correct (Brier score 0.240).

cost.quote: stage-1 sessions lasting a median of 6 (batch) to 9 (interactive) minutes.
Stage-2 sessions used a median of 7.5 of their 50 forward passes (range 1–35).

baselines_and_controls: 10 clean models (false-alarm control); oracle retraining; fine-tuning dense layers on clean labelled windows; interpretability pipeline (TF-MoDISco-lite + TomTom + zeroing filters); random edits matched in count/magnitude (0 of 520 fixed).
runs_and_variance: 56 sessions (28 models x 2 stages), each model once per stage; cluster bootstrap (10,000 resamples) CIs; Holm correction; two blind coders with kappa = 1.000; within-model consistency kappa = 0.60.
robustness_of_edits: not tested beyond clean test AUPRC and probe metrics
verification: statistical: preregistration with 13 amendments, blinded coding, cluster bootstrap; audits for gradients, network use, access outside run directory, and static counting of local forward computation
memorization_vs_reasoning: Detection did not come from weights alone: every correct detection came from sessions that ran network parts locally. Author notes 'detection from weights alone' was neither shown nor refuted; planned follow-up gives weights as text with no tools.
limitations_stated: Four plant instances only; one model family for design, harness, subjects and coders; mid-study rule change (Amendment 3) keeping 24 input-layer runs that broke instructions; self-selected compliance; infrastructure session knew answer key and had documented blinding slips.
code_or_data: https://github.com/brunicardoso/weight-space-programming-genomics/tree/v1.0.1 ; Zenodo zip (answer keys, weights, transcripts withheld for blinded follow-up)
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. 2026 Sparks of WSP [5] and complete logs [6]
notes_for_survey: Preregistered, blinded B1 reading/backdoor-detection test with clean controls; documents that 'no forward pass' conditions can be bypassed by agents computing layers locally, which accompanied every correct detection. Repairs were conservative and rarely met a strict fix criterion.
